chapter: Bantan Sango Case File: The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light
act_title: Bantan Sango Case File: The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light

quests.title: Bantan Sango Case File: The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light

dialogue.t: Oh, you're right on cue.
I just finished scouting out several suspicious spots.
One of those encampments is guarded by the "Top"...
Ahem. I mean, by "Black Shadow." If you've got no other questions...
As for that, I don't know anything at the moment.
Eh!? Didn't Sango get you to go investigate?
She did, yes, but... How should I put it?
For example, "some overripe Lavender Melons" and "muddy hand-prints on a door" don't connect meaningfully in my mind.
But for Sango, these are the materials she needs to unlock mysteries as complex as "yosegizaiku."
"Some overripe Lavender Melons" and "muddy hand-prints on a door"... How are these related, actually?
I'm just using an analogy. At her direction, I investigated some locations in Yashiori Island and Chinju Forest before reporting what I had seen back to her.
As for any conclusions she might have drawn from my reports, only she knows what they are.
To be honest, only Shikanoin is able to keep up with her train of thought...
Someone from the Tenryou Commission. We had the privilege of making his acquaintance on a previous case.
He's a rather... unique character. You'll know what I mean should you ever meet him.
Well then. The animals are in your hands.
Paimon's still thinking about those "overripe Lavender Melons"...
I will continue to investigate "Black Shadow." The matter of the small animals is yours to resolve.
Don't worry, I've already made some initial deductions. Ryuuji will continue to investigate "Black Shadow," while you will focus on rescuing those animals.
Ah. Wonderful! This should be all of them now...
...Wait. Why *isn't* it all of them?
Uh-oh... Why does Paimon feel like this is just dragging out?
It is true that resolving cases sometimes requires a great deal of patience. Going the wrong way could end with you finding nothing at all.
We have found a great deal of these little animals, so we are at least headed in the right direction.
We might just have missed a few clues along the way or left a few locations un-searched, thus leading to our current impasse. It will be a temporary one, I believe.
Ooh, Paimon gets it! You're saying that we'll need a bit of boom shaka-laka to finally clear this up!
Mm, yes, you could say that we are presently boom shaka-lacking. But not by much, I would say — we have been making great progress thanks to the two of you.

dialogue.sit: (It feels like he already understands you pretty well, Paimon...)

dialogue.t: That makes a ton of sense, Ryuuji!
You flatter me. This is merely experience talking.
The further down the truth is buried, the more value there is in uncovering it.
It's just a shame that we don't have any additional information at the moment. Hmm...
I suppose I'll simply report our present status to Sango.
She should be able to consider some angles that haven't come to mind yet.
Sure! Paimon has faith in your good sense, after all!
Then it's decided. Let's meet at the usual place once more clues emerge.
If I am otherwise occupied at the time, you can just look for Sango directly.

quests.description: Ryuuji seems to have gotten further leads and must investigate once more…
